steps.content: You free your feet from the sucking mud and kick loose rubble aside. The handkerchief Lichen gave you works across your face, scrubbing away grime, but it can't erase the ashy taste of talisman water still clinging to your senses. At least your head feels clearer. A little.

You raise your eyes to the ruins. They stand silent, hollow. In the distance, white fog unfurls, curling through cracks in the brickwork like breath, like something alive. Something watches from within, a gaze thick with ill intent.
And through it all, one person wanders utterly unconcerned.
[Lichen's portrait]

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The Dao dwells in breath, the heart neighbors the void. In stillness, illumination; in illumination, eternal tranquility...
The cyan-robed Daoist moves through the endless fog, leisurely as a dream, her soft chanting accompanied by the gentle ring of the bell. Wherever the sound reaches, the mournful wails simply cease.
Wisps of low gray cloud drift near her. She notices them, smiles, and flicks her sleeve. The gust disperses them like thought. She walks on, untouched by mud, unmarked by the mire.
Then, as if feeling your gaze, she turns. Her eyes find yours, transfixed as you are. And her serene expression breaks, blooms, and becomes a smile meant just for you.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Mm... Where the bell chimes, evil spirits retreat. Everything within a hundred meters is as safe as can be.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hehe. Look at that face. "This doesn't make any sense." What, seeing's still not believing? You won't accept that Daoism has its own divine arts?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Do I really have to drag you to the Tianyi Sect and make you learn a few tricks before you see the light?
You say nothing. Instead, you slide half a step back until the cold wall presses against your spine.

Divine arts. Right. You've seen strange things before—demons, monsters, things wearing friendly faces. You haven't forgotten. You won't be fooled by a pleasant smile and a clean robe. And you're certainly not about to start asking questions like some trusting fool.
She doesn't seem to mind your silence. She simply continues talking, unhurried, as if she has all the time in the world.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I came on urgent business; knew I couldn't go it alone. Cast a divination, seeking aid, followed the signs... and they led me straight to you, young friend. What I didn't expect was...

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...that the good kid everyone praises so highly would sneak out of camp, wander into a forbidden zone, and end up sprawled out in the mud. Took some doing to wake you, I'll have you know.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: So what's the story? Our famously clever little guide, sharp as a blade—lost? Were you sleepwalking? Homesick, maybe?
She leans down, hand reaching for your head. You dodge.
The question is out before you can stop it, and you immediately regret it. The recognition in her eyes is unmistakable.
She cocks an eyebrow, gaze sharpening as she studies you through narrowed lids. You lick your lips and offer nothing.
To your relief, she doesn't push. Just a small, knowing smile, and she picks up where she left off.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: A foreign name can't be that hard to remember... This is the last time I'll remind you. Forget it again, and I might just be heartbroken.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: This humble one's surname is Li, given name Xianling. I go by Lichen. Disciple of the Tianyi Sect, seeker of the Dao from the Eastern Continent, and part-time consultant for a certain expedition.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Same as you, I'm a special guest, invited by the scientists.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That's right. The ■ Nation on the eastern coast. Tens of thousands of miles across the sea. Fastest voyage takes well over ten days, and if the weather turns, well, fish gotta eat. So you see...
She reaches for your head again. You try to dodge, but the wall is right there. Your head thumps against it just as her finger connects with your brow.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: To meet you here, of all places? We must be kindred spirits. Blessed by the heavens.
Your eyes trace her features, her clothing. There's something familiar about them; she looks like the Eastians you've known.
Which means... if this truly is the expedition era, the early N.F. 20s... then you've encountered others like her before...

steps.speaker: Yingying
steps.content: Eastia? Where's that?
A time before Eastia, before the city-states, when their people were divided into nations... the Eastern Continent?
You could ask. The questions burn on your tongue. Instead, you hold them in. You watch her in silence, spine against the cold wall, refusing to come closer.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That look... Are you thinking, "Why'd the scientists bring along some mystical charlatan spouting nonsense"?
...You said no such thing. You have no desire to converse with her. But then you see her pinch her fingers together, assuming an air of enigmatic wisdom.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hmph, rude little one. Show some respect. The Dao of Heaven is in disarray—Yin and Yang all thrown off balance—those fancy Western formulas of the expedition aren't half as useful as my Daoist arts. Take just now, for instance...

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Without the pure chime of my bell, you'd probably still be weeping away in that nightmare.
...You weren't crying.
That was—
You try to recall that blurry and dreadful dream, yet find no words to describe it. She watches you with keen interest for a moment before her expression turns serious.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: From the look of it... you just entered the <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That's what the Tianyi Sect calls it. The <color=#fb9259>Realm of Yang</color> and the <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>—two sides of the same ruins. The little curly-haired one came up with a name too, but it was such a mouthful I forgot it. Helen and her lot have a simpler Western way of putting it: <color=#fb9259>reality</color> and its shadow, <color=#fb9259>dream</color>.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: When that baleful star fell from the heavens, every living thing in this lakeside town vanished overnight. In their place, things unseen and unspeakable gathered slowly. Beyond reality. Within dreams. And built themselves a city of ghosts and spirits.

"Ghosts and spirits"... She means the Manic Entities, doesn't she? The ones that wore false faces and tried to take you. It's not a bad word for them. They were insubstantial as smoke, yet touched with something deeply uncanny.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Ghosts and spirits commune with heaven and earth. Transcend past and present. Omniscient. Omnipotent. Close to the Dao of Heaven itself. So... the slightest stir on their side ripples through all things on ours.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: This is the ruins of <color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>. We, the living, dwell on its Yang side. Ghosts and spirits keep watch in the Void of Yin. The baleful star bridged the two. And the expedition... they came seeking that hidden path.
<color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>... This place again.
...Have you been to the Void of Yin too? Did you find an entrance?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I was just about to ask you the same thing.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin are two separate worlds. Ordinary people can neither see nor touch the other side. Force your way in recklessly, and you only invite disaster. I've dreamed of it once or twice. Not even sure those were real. But you...

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Only a rare few with extraordinary gifts, and the right fate, can enter the ruined city, close their eyes, take a nap, and slip right into the Void of Yin. I'm green with envy, I tell you.
Envy? You stare at her, incredulous. Those twisted stone statues, those paper effigies—each one more disturbing than the last. You couldn't even tell what they were. Human? Object? Dead? Alive?
You breathe deep and look at her again. Really look. The patterns on her robe are nearly identical to what the "dead" wore. The one in your dream who commanded shadows to attack you.
Coincidence? It can't be. Then what is she really after, coming here for this <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Alright then, tell me: what did you see in the Void of Yin just now, young friend?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Someone who could control ghosts... Someone dead.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: The clothes that person wore… looked a lot like… yours.
You let the final word hang in the air, heavy with intention, and watch.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...Looked like mine? Could it be...
Lichen's eyes brighten, alive with interest. She leans in half a step, sleeves drifting with the movement.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You saw my shifu?!
...Shifu?
She doesn't answer you, already lost in her own joy.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I knew it. She's here. Right here. All that searching, it wasn't for nothing!

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Here, let me give you a proper introduction. My shifu's name is—ah, never mind, you won't remember it anyway. Point is, she's the grandmaster of the Tianyi Sect. Great mystic of the ■ Nation, Eastern Continent.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Decades ago, she was already performing divinations and exorcisms for the people online. Training an exceptional disciple, namely, me. Amassing tens of thousands of fans... I mean, devoted believers.
...They had online influencer scams in this Eastern Continent a century ago?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You're thinking something rude again, aren't you? That my shifu's a fraud just like me? Uh-uh. Different. She has real talent.
Did she just admit... she really is a fraud?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Years before the Nightfall, my shifu had already divined the <color=#fb9259>Perishing Star</color>'s arrival.
Your reaction clearly delights her. She gives her head a slow, dramatic shake, then carries on with her tale.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The prophecy came true. Calamities swept the land. A few years later, my shifu vanished without a word. Her followers believed she'd passed on. But recently, she started appearing in my dreams. In the dreams of many others.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: She said nothing. But I know... she is in the Void of Yin. She has attained the Dao of Heaven. Transcended life and death. And she wishes for us to find her.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Well? Interested? Come find her with me. The divination is never wrong. You, young friend, are the one I must rely on for this journey. I'll be the advisor, you be the guide. I'll ward off your misfortune; you lead the way. What do you say?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Once we find my shifu, the good karma will be first-rate!
She pats your shoulder, leaning close. And in her eyes, you catch a flicker not of fear, but of something rawer. Longing... perhaps?
You've seen that look before. In someone else's eyes.
No. You force the thought away. Here, now, in this place, dwelling on <color=#fb9259>her</color> is dangerous. It will only sink you further.
I have no interest in good karma, and I have no plan of going back. I don't want to get tangled up in things I can't understand. No wish to take that kind of risk. Ever again.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The greater the risk, the richer the fortune! For seekers of the Dao like myself, glimpsing truth through danger? That's the blessing we dream of.
Easy for you to say. That place can cost you your life.
If you want to know what I learned there, what it taught me, it's this:
Stay far away. Never dream of asking them for anything. One wrong word, and there's no turning back.
I will never go back to that place—
The bell at her waist draws your gaze like a moth to flame. You try to look away—command yourself to—but your eyes won't obey. Your hands are shaking. You didn't even notice until now.
Silence hangs above you for a long moment. Then, soft as breath, a sigh.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...But where in this world is not dangerous?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: These are not fortunate times. Anyone with aspirations must steel their resolve. Be ready for sacrifice.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Look at you—this expedition, venturing into ruined towns and abandoned cities. Was that all just to stay safe?
Words fail you. What could you possibly say? To her, you're just a child who wandered off from the group and stumbled into Maria City like a fool. If you tried to explain...
...No. You stop yourself. You don't owe her an explanation.

options: I don't want anything from this place.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I don't seek danger. I don't seek what I can't get. I just want to leave.
She gazes at you quietly for a moment, then lets out a soft chuckle.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...Alright. I'll stop pushing you.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: No matter how gifted you are, young friend, you're still a child at heart. Knowing fear is a good thing, especially in a place like this. I can tell you've been through far too many frights.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Rest assured. There is still one last safe place in this world.
Mid-sentence, she pulls a long hairpin from her hair. A casual gesture, unhurried.
Behind her, a scratching sound begins, faint at first, then insistent. Like claws on wood. Like something trying to get out. Fog seeps from the shadows ahead, taking shape.
She doesn't turn. Just lifts her hand, sleeve falling back to reveal her wrist, and flicks.
The hairpin pierces the forehead of the monster formed from fog.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Stay by my side. I'll keep you safe.
